correctness.rationale: For a vertex subset F of K_m,n with u>0 left and v>0 right vertices, induced degrees are v on left and u on right; maximum degree≤r iff u,v≤r. Pure left or right faces are unrestricted. Thus the degree-bound complex equals (A*B) union Delta_L union Delta_R, where A and B are (r-1)-skeleta of the respective full simplices. Skeleton reduced integral H_(r-1) is Λ^r W_m, respectively Λ^r W_n: exterior simplicial boundary is contraction by the coordinate-sum augmentation, and its degree-r kernel is Λ^r ker(epsilon), a free integral lattice of binomial rank. The skeleta are homotopy equivalent to wedges of spheres in dimension r-1 via explicit acyclic cone-vertex matching. Their join A*B is a wedge of ab spheres of dimension 2r-1; both inclusions A,B into J=A*B are nullhomotopic because each is coned by an opposite-part vertex. Attaching the two contractible full simplices thus splits nonequivariantly as J∨ΣA∨ΣB, yielding (a+b) S^r and ab S^(2r-1) for a=C(m-1,r), b=C(n-1,r). The long exact sequence of (D_r,J) identifies degree-r integral modules with Λ^r W_m⊕Λ^r W_n, and degree-(2r-1) with their tensor product; r≥2 avoids degree collision. Swapping balanced parts interchanges the degree-r summands and acts on top join cycles as (-1)^((r-1+1)^2)=(-1)^r tensor flip. Character formulas follow from exterior-power traces and tr((P⊗Q)Flip)=tr(PQ). Source finite modular and signed Lefschetz tests support small instances, but the general family follows analytically.
residual_risks: Splitting is NONEQUIVARIANT; equivariance holds only for integral homology modules and balanced part-exchange sign.
The exceptional r=1 extension case is excluded; no general noncomplete bipartite graph assertion is made.

value.rationale: A natural induced-degree filtration of complete bipartite graphs has a uniform, exact and surprisingly mixed-dimensional integral homotopy type for all r≥2 with a closed, nontrivial equivariant homology representation and parity-sensitive part-swap. This classification goes well beyond the known numerical maximum independent set size and provides precise invariants for an infinite graph family, rather than an unmotivated finite slice.
residual_risks: No claim for r=1 or arbitrary bipartite graphs; equivalent classical join theorem applied elsewhere remains possible.

limitations: No independent replay of all finite test instances; general proof is analytic and does not rely on finite checks.
